newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's unemployment rises to 9.9 pct in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Canada's unemployment rises to 9.9 pct in Sept.

text.p: Statistics Canada said on Friday the unemployment rate rose to 9.9 percent in September from 9.4 percent in August.
Note - Labor force, employment and unemployment in millions, on seasonally adjusted basis.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the unemployment rate to drop to 9.3 percent and employment to grow by 37,000 in September.
Full-time employment fell by 86,000, wiping out the 72,000 gain in August and cutting the year's total gains in half. Part-time employment rose by 39,000 in September.

Statistics Canada said three quarters of the overall employment decline occurred in Ontario. Employment in Canada's richest province fell by 35,000, partly offsetting the 82,000 jobs created in the two previous months.

Statistics Canada said all of the job losses in September were in the service producing industries, which lost 48,000 jobs in the month. A drop of 70,000 in community, business and personal services wiped out all the employment gains so far this year, the agency said.
Employment rose by 20,000 in finance, insurance and real estate.

The total number of jobs created so far this year fell to 106,000 in September from 153,000 in August. Statistics Canada said employment in the goods producing industries had risen 94,000 since the beginning of the year.
Statistics Canada said manufacturing had led the way in job creation this year, with 104,000 jobs created so far.
"Most of the increase has taken place over the past six months, during which employment increased by 5.3 percent and hours worked rose by 4.3 percent," the agency said.

Employment in Quebec, which lost 41,000 jobs in June and 35,000 jobs in July before gaining 41,000 jobs in August, remained little changed in September. Overall, Canada's French-speaking province lost 26,000 jobs since December 1995, Statistics Canada said.
